subproblem.title: Closure theorem for compactly supported sequences (CL*), degree d + 1 < P: reduction to cycles (parent V3, V4, V15)
subproblem.statement: Assume (MR), (IMC), (VO) (types of the accepted cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, dtc_vanish_off_support) and (Isor) (verbatim the second conjunct of sibling deformation). Let P, d ∈ ℕ with d + 1 < P and assume CL_P(d) and BR_P(d) (as in sibling boundary_im). Then CL*_{P,d+1}: if K ⊆ ℝ^P is compact and T_j ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) are IM with IM boundaries, spt T_j ⊆ K for all j, sup_j(M(T_j) + M(∂T_j)) < ∞ and T_j ⇀ T, then T is IM.

B)) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α)) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → (∀ (P m : ℕ), m + 1 < P → ∃ c : ℝ, 1 ≤ c ∧ ∀ Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Z → IsCompact Z.support → Z.boundary = 0 → Z.mass < ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ Y.boundary = Z ∧ Y.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * (2 * c * Z.mass.toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (m + 1)) * Z.mass.toReal) ∧ Y.support ⊆ thickening (3 * Real.sqrt P * (2 * c * Z.mass.toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (m + 1))) Z.support) → ∀ (P d : ℕ), d + 1 < P → (∀ (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U d) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U d), IsOpen U → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + boundaryMassOn (Ts j) W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T) → (∀ (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : GeometricCurrentOn U (d + 1)), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity R → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → R.boundary.massOn W < ∞) → IsIntegerMultiplicity R.boundary) → (∀ (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j).boundary) → (∀ j, (Ts j).support ⊆ K) → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).mass + (Ts j).boundary.mass) < ∞ → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent V3, V4(o), V4(i) and V15. Uses (SL), (RU), (REP), (MM) and the siblings slice_limit (SLIM_{P,d} from CL_P(d)), lower_density (LD_{P,d}) and cycle_im (CYC_{P,d}). n := d + 1.
1. spt T ⊆ K by (VO); M(T), M(∂T) < ∞ by lower semicontinuity; ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T.
2. ∂T is IM: CL_P(d) in U := ℝ^P for the ∂T_j (boundaryMassOn(∂T_j, W) = 0).
3. Filling. If n ≥ 2, (Isor) with m := d − 1 gives an IM Y with ∂Y = ∂T and compact support. If n = 1, ∂T = Σm_i⟨·(x_i)⟩ is a finite integer point sum in K ((MR), (VO)), Σm_i = ∂T(ζ) = lim_j T_j(dζ) = 0 for ζ = 1 near K, and Y := Σm_i[[x₀, x_i]] (IM oriented segments with ∂[[x₀, x]] = ⟨·(x)⟩ − ⟨·(x₀)⟩) works.
4. Γ := T − Y is a cycle with compact support and finite mass.
5. If X and ∂X are IM with finite masses then X has ISP: for admissible representations and f, (SL) gives slices Z_t with locally finite mass for a.e. t ((MM)); A_t = X⌞{f<t} is IM by (IMC)(b) and (RU), likewise B_t; ∂A_t = B_t + Z_t has locally finite mass, so it is IM by BR_P(d) in ℝ^P, and Z_t = ∂A_t − B_t is IM by (IMC)(c).
6. Hence every T_j and Y have ISP, and SLIM_{P,d} (sibling slice_limit) gives ISP(T).
7. Γ has ISP: by (RU) applied to T = Γ + Y and ∂T = ∂Γ + ∂Y, the slices satisfy ∂A − B = Z^T_t − Z^Y_t, which is IM by (IMC)(c) for a.e. t.
8. LD_{P,d} (sibling lower_density) and CYC_{P,d} (sibling cycle_im) show that Γ is IM; T = Γ − (0 − Y) is IM by (IMC)(c). ∎
Note: accepted cbr_cc_* and cbr_ccisp_* declarations cover steps 3 (n = 1), 5 and 7.
proof_key_steps: ∂T IM and a compact IM filling Y of ∂T.
ISP of T_j, Y and T, hence of Γ := T − Y.
LD and CYC make Γ and T IM.

audit.reason: CL_P(d) proves integrality of the limit boundary. The positive-degree filling or zero-dimensional segment construction produces Y; slice linearity and the supplied limit theorem give ISP for T−Y. The cycle criterion then proves precisely the stated compact-support closure result.
